description: Add categories the document does not have — **a list of them in one call**. `choose_categories` only keeps or archives the ones already there, so this is what answers "none of these fit". Give a `parent_id` or `parent_name` to put it under another, in which case it takes the parent’s kind and `kind` is ignored. Categories nest three levels at most (Living → Utilities → Electricity): a top-level category is a heading — Living, Lifestyle, Income — and a Plan bucket for it counts everything under it. Entries are applied in order, so a parent and its children go in the same call. If a category of the same name already sits in the same place nothing is created: a live one is reported back with its id, an archived one is brought back rather than twinned. Writes immediately — the change is additive, so there is nothing to preview.

categories.description: One entry per category. Up to 100 in a call.

kind.description: One of EXPENSE, INCOME, TRANSFER, SAVING, DEBT_PAYMENT. Defaults to EXPENSE. Ignored for a subcategory.

name.description: The name as the user would say it. `Groceries`, not a path.

parent_id.description: The category this one goes under. Ids from `category_tree`.

parent_name.description: The parent by name (or path) instead of by id — including one created earlier in this same call.

path.description: Absolute path to a .emd file on this machine.

name: create_category
title: Create categories
